brief: Goldman Sachs' 2027 global outlook argues a friendly macro baseline (stable growth, falling inflation, peaking policy rates) collides with an ageing market cycle: real rates, credit spreads and volatility are all rising, and the AI investment impulse, which has driven more of the gain in market value and earnings than in GDP, is forecast to peak in early 2027, a bigger test for markets than for the economy. GS sees two ways this stays orderly: 2027 S&P 500 earnings growth, though slower than 2026's 36%, stays a robust 11%, and gains can pass from AI infrastructure names to hyperscalers, productivity beneficiaries or non-AI firms. The risk is that the market looks further ahead or financial conditions tighten, turning a rotation into a bigger shock. Other calls: oil's baseline is a gradual decline, with an Iran-escalation spike the main near-term risk. GS turns more bullish on duration (10y UST at 4.6% by end-2027) and expects a roughly 3% Dollar decline, led by JPY and CNY gains. US credit spreads widen further on AI financing strain. EM's case shifts from direction to diversified yield, and equity-index volatility has room to rise further.

cards.claim: Goldman Sachs' 2027 macro baseline is stable growth, declining inflation and peaking policy rates, which it calls a friendly backdrop even as the market cycle ages.
cards.anchor: Our headline macro forecasts for 2027 are quite friendly: stable growth, declining inflation and peaking policy rates

cards.claim: Goldman Sachs says the broader risk-asset picture is more two-sided than it has been in several years, arguing for more diversified, better-hedged portfolios.
